\section[o fusível]{o fusível — the fuse}

\label{lesson:PT-C432-fusivel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the thermostat, then the Portuguese for to air.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o fusível}
\textbf{o fusível} — \textquotedblleft{}the fuse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Saltou um fusível e a cozinha ficou sem luz.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A fuse blew and the kitchen lost its lights.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Saltar} — to blow, of a fuse or a breaker.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fusível} came from French \emph{fusible} 'that can melt', built on Latin \emph{fūsus}, from \emph{fundere} 'to melt, to pour' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o fusível}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o fusível}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o fusível}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the thermostat, then the Portuguese for to air, then say \emph{o fusível} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o fusível mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The fuse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[fundir]{fundir — to blow out (of a bulb or fuse); to melt; to merge}

\label{lesson:PT-C432-fundir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to air, then the Portuguese for the fuse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fundir}
\textbf{fundir} — \textquotedblleft{}to blow out (of a bulb or fuse); to melt; to merge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A lâmpada da casa de banho fundiu-se.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The bathroom bulb has blown.}
\end{quote}

For a bulb, \emph{fundir-se} is the usual form. It also means to merge: \emph{as duas empresas fundiram-se}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fundir} comes from Latin \emph{fundere} 'to pour, to melt' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fundir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fundir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fundir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to air, then the Portuguese for the fuse, then say \emph{fundir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does fundir mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To blow out (of a bulb or fuse); to melt; to merge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o disjuntor]{o disjuntor — the circuit breaker}

\label{lesson:PT-C432-disjuntor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the fuse, then the Portuguese for to blow out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o disjuntor}
\textbf{o disjuntor} — \textquotedblleft{}the circuit breaker\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O disjuntor desligou quando liguei o forno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The circuit breaker tripped when I turned on the oven.}
\end{quote}

People also say \emph{o quadro} for the box of breakers.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{disjuntor} came from French \emph{disjoncteur}, built on Latin \emph{disiungere} 'to unyoke, to separate', on \emph{iungere} 'to join' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o disjuntor}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o disjuntor}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o disjuntor}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the fuse, then the Portuguese for to blow out, then say \emph{o disjuntor} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o disjuntor mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The circuit breaker\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[recarregar]{recarregar — to recharge; to reload}

\label{lesson:PT-C432-recarregar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to blow out, then the Portuguese for the circuit breaker.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: recarregar}
\textbf{recarregar} — \textquotedblleft{}to recharge; to reload\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Recarrego o telemóvel durante a noite.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I recharge my phone overnight.}
\end{quote}

Also to top up a travel card: \emph{recarregar o passe}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{recarregar} is built from \emph{re-} and \emph{carregar} 'to load' (EtymDB), which goes back to Latin \emph{carrus} 'cart'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{recarregar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{recarregar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{recarregar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to blow out, then the Portuguese for the circuit breaker, then say \emph{recarregar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does recarregar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To recharge; to reload\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o apagão]{o apagão — the power cut, the blackout}

\label{lesson:PT-C432-apagao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the circuit breaker, then the Portuguese for to recharge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o apagão}
\textbf{o apagão} — \textquotedblleft{}the power cut, the blackout\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Houve um apagão em todo o bairro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There was a power cut in the whole neighbourhood.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{apagar}, to switch off.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{apagão} is built on \emph{apagar} 'to put out, to switch off' with \emph{-ão}; \emph{apagar} goes back to Latin \emph{pācāre} 'to calm, to pacify' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o apagão}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o apagão}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o apagão}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the circuit breaker, then the Portuguese for to recharge, then say \emph{o apagão} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o apagão mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The power cut, the blackout\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Revisão dos capítulos 425–432}

\label{lesson:PT-R432-revisao-425-432}



\begin{quote}
Say the Portuguese for the hostel and the country inn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the hostel, the country inn, the roadside inn, the guesthouse, camping
  \item to camp, the caravan, the camper van, the tent peg, the mosquito net
  \item the security deposit, to call off, the cancellation, to bring forward, to rebook
  \item the accommodation, to spend the night, the overnight stay, to put up, the doorman
  \item the cot, the pillowcase, the hair dryer, the coat hanger, the bathrobe
  \item to drip, the drain, to block, to unblock, the toilet cistern
  \item the radiator, the heater, the water heater, the thermostat, to air
  \item the fuse, to blow out, the circuit breaker, to recharge, the power cut
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The hostel? (\textbf{o albergue}.) The country inn? (\textbf{a pousada}.) The roadside inn? (\textbf{a estalagem}.) The guesthouse? (\textbf{a residencial}.) Camping? (\textbf{o campismo}.) To camp? (\textbf{acampar}.) The caravan? (\textbf{a caravana}.) The camper van? (\textbf{a autocaravana}.) The tent peg? (\textbf{a estaca}.) The mosquito net? (\textbf{o mosquiteiro}.) The security deposit? (\textbf{a caução}.) To call off? (\textbf{desmarcar}.) The cancellation? (\textbf{o cancelamento}.) To bring forward? (\textbf{antecipar}.) To rebook? (\textbf{remarcar}.) The accommodation? (\textbf{o alojamento}.) To spend the night? (\textbf{pernoitar}.) The overnight stay? (\textbf{a dormida}.) To put up? (\textbf{hospedar}.) The doorman? (\textbf{o porteiro}.) The cot? (\textbf{o berço}.) The pillowcase? (\textbf{a fronha}.) The hair dryer? (\textbf{o secador}.) The coat hanger? (\textbf{o cabide}.) The bathrobe? (\textbf{o roupão}.) To drip? (\textbf{pingar}.) The drain? (\textbf{o ralo}.) To block? (\textbf{entupir}.) To unblock? (\textbf{desentupir}.) The toilet cistern? (\textbf{o autoclismo}.) The radiator? (\textbf{o radiador}.) The heater? (\textbf{o aquecedor}.) The water heater? (\textbf{o esquentador}.) The thermostat? (\textbf{o termóstato}.) To air? (\textbf{arejar}.) The fuse? (\textbf{o fusível}.) To blow out? (\textbf{fundir}.) The circuit breaker? (\textbf{o disjuntor}.) To recharge? (\textbf{recarregar}.) The power cut? (\textbf{o apagão}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
